samples.summary: `clearAuthCookies` never expires the `__Host-` session cookies when the deployment is currently non-`Secure`, so a signed-out JWT/refresh token can be resurrected
samples.evidence: The sweep is `new Set([sessionCookieName(), refreshCookieName(), ...UNPREFIXED_SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES])`. `UNPREFIXED_SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES` (oauth-state.ts:104) holds only the *bare* names. So when `useSecureCookies()` is false, `sessionCookieName()`/`refreshCookieName()` also return the bare names and the set degenerates to `{wafflebase_session, wafflebase_refresh}` — `__Host-wafflebase_session` / `__Host-wafflebase_refresh` are never cleared. Vector: a deployment runs https (`__Host-` cookies issued, refresh cookie maxAge 7d, JWTs are stateless with no server-side revocation), then flips to non-`Secure` (`COOKIE_SECURE=false`, or `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` reverted to `http://` behind a TLS proxy). A user calls `POST /auth/logout`; it answers 200 but the `__Host-` refresh cookie survives in the browser. On the next flip back to `Secure`, `refreshCookieName()` again resolves to `__Host-wafflebase_refresh`, the surviving cookie is sent, and `POST /auth/refresh` mints a fresh session for an account that was signed out — up to 7 days later. The doc-block above the function and docs/design/backend.md both claim sign-out expires the cookies "in both their prefixed and unprefixed names"; the sweep is only symmetric in one direction. Fix: build the set from both the prefixed and unprefixed constants unconditionally.

samples.summary: Session/refresh cookies lose `Secure` (and `__Host-`) on a TLS-terminated deployment whose `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` is still `http://` — a downgrade from the previous `NODE_ENV==='production'` rule
samples.evidence: `isSecureCookie()` now returns `false` for any `http://` callback URL *even under `NODE_ENV=production`* (line 238), and `AuthController.baseCookieOptions()` (auth.controller.ts:406) feeds that straight into the session and refresh cookies, which previously used `secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'`. packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42 and :124-140 hand operators exactly this shape (`GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL=http://your-domain:3000/auth/github/callback`) and the shipped image sets `NODE_ENV=production`. Such a deployment sitting behind an https-terminating proxy silently starts emitting the session JWT and the 7-day refresh token without `Secure` and without `__Host-`: any plaintext http request to the same host (a typed `http://` URL, an injected http subresource) exposes them to a network attacker, and any sibling-subdomain foothold can now write `wafflebase_session; Domain=<parent>` — the very session-fixation the same commit says `__Host-` exists to stop. The only compensation is a single `logger.warn` reached exclusively through `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` (github-auth.guard.ts:263), i.e. only if someone starts a GitHub login on that process; deployments authenticating from existing cookies or API keys never see it. Consider defaulting to `Secure` when `NODE_ENV=production` unless `COOKIE_SECURE=false` is explicit, rather than letting a stale callback URL silently downgrade.

samples.summary: `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` is documented as the key the OAuth login bindings are signed with (HKDF of `JWT_SECRET`), but nothing in the code reads it and the state is an unkeyed SHA-256
samples.evidence: packages/backend/README.md:25 and the env table added to docs/design/backend.md both describe `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` — "Key the OAuth login bindings are signed with… HKDF of JWT_SECRET… set it to an independent value to remove any relation between the `state` an unauthenticated `GET /auth/github` publishes and the session-signing key." A repo-wide grep for `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET`, `hkdf` and `bindingSecret` across `packages/` returns only that README line: no source file reads the variable, and `createWebOAuthState`/`webOAuthStateMatches` (oauth-state.ts:165-185) use `hashSecret()` = plain unkeyed `sha256`, with no HMAC anywhere in the auth module except `cliConfirmToken`. An operator who sets `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` believing they have separated the OAuth-binding key from `JWT_SECRET` gets no such separation, silently. Either implement the derivation or remove the variable from the docs.

samples.summary: `SENSITIVE_PARAMS` lists names the application never uses (`code_challenge`, `cli_confirm`) and omits the ones it does (`challenge`, `confirm`, `verifier`)
samples.evidence: The CLI login start is `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=…&nonce=…&challenge=…` and the consent link is `?confirm=<HMAC>` (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:193-197) — the real parameter names are `challenge` and `confirm`, neither of which is in the set, while `code_challenge` and `cli_confirm` (names that appear nowhere in the routing) are. Today these values only ever ride under `/auth`, where the whole query is dropped by `isAuthPath`, so the gap is defence-in-depth rather than a live leak; but the set is the *only* thing protecting them on any path that misses the `/auth` prefix test — e.g. an absolute-form request line (`GET http://host/auth/github?challenge=…`), which `isAuthPath` rejects because the normalized string does not start with `/auth`, and which then falls through to `redactParams` where `challenge` is not matched. Add `challenge`, `confirm` and `verifier` to the set.

samples.summary: `login-url.txt` holds a live login credential; it is written through a follow-symlink `writeFileSync` and is not removed if the process is interrupted
samples.evidence: `announceLoginUrl` does `rmSync(file, {force:true})` then `writeFileSync(file, url, {mode: 0o600})` (lines 156-157). `writeFileSync` opens with `'w'`, which follows symlinks, so anything that can create an entry at `dirname(getConfigPath())/login-url.txt` between the unlink and the create — trivially so when `WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG` points at a shared directory, as the new tests do with `tmpdir()` — receives this login's `nonce` and PKCE `challenge`, which the surrounding comments correctly describe as a credential. Using `flag: 'wx'` would fail closed on a pre-planted symlink. Separately, the file is deleted only in the `finally` around `await waitForCallback()` (line 365); a SIGINT/SIGTERM during the five-minute wait skips it, leaving the live URL on disk for the remainder of the backend's state TTL.

samples.summary: The launch-token indirection moves the secret one hop but does not remove it from argv-readable reach; docs claim more than it delivers
samples.evidence: `armLaunch` returns `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/launch/<32-byte token>` and that URL is what `open()` puts in the opener child's argv (line 351). A local user who reads argv can still `GET` it and receive a 302 whose `Location` is the full authorization URL with `nonce` and `challenge` (lines 658-670). Single use means the victim then sees the 410 page instead of a silent compromise — a real improvement — but docs/design/cli.md's "The authorization URL never reaches argv or a log" reads as though the bindings are protected from a local reader, which they are not; the property actually gained is detectability, not confidentiality. Worth stating accurately so the next change does not lean on the stronger claim.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as the reviewer describes. `clearAuthCookies` (auth.controller.ts:349-361) sweeps `new Set([sessionCookieName(), refreshCookieName(), ...UNPREFIXED_SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES])`, and `UNPREFIXED_SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES` (oauth-state.ts:104-107) contains only the bare `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh`. Because `sessionCookieName()`/`refreshCookieName()` (oauth-state.ts:89-95 via hostPrefixedCookieName at 62-64) return the bare names whenever `isSecureCookie()` is false, the set degenerates to the two bare names and the `__Host-`-prefixed cookies are never expired — the sweep is symmetric in only one direction, contradicting its own doc-block (auth.controller.ts:343-347) and oauth-state.ts:84. The vector completes: `isSecureCookie()` (oauth-state.ts:230-239) flips to false on `COOKIE_SECURE=false` or an `http://` GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL even while the origin is still https behind a TLS proxy (so the `secure:true` clear would otherwise have landed); `POST /auth/logout` (auth.controller.ts:86-90) does nothing but call clearAuthCookies and return 200; refresh tokens are stateless with no revocation (auth.service.ts:124-134), and `POST /auth/refresh` (auth.controller.ts:262-300) reads `req.cookies[refreshCookieName()]` and mints a fresh session. So a surviving `__Host-wafflebase_refresh` (7-day max-age, auth.controller.ts:376-382) re-authenticates an account that was signed out once the config flips back to Secure. No caller-side or config-side guard prevents this; the nearest related code is a test asserting current behavior (auth.controller.spec.ts:490-529), not a guard. In lane (auth/session revocation) and blocking under the security rubric.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim checks out. `isSecureCookie()` (oauth-state.ts:229-240) returns false for any `http://` GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL at line 238, short-circuiting before the `NODE_ENV === 'production'` fallback at line 239, so a production install behind a TLS-terminating proxy that still carries an `http://` callback URL loses `Secure`. The same predicate gates `__Host-` prefixing for the session and refresh cookies (oauth-state.ts:62-95), and `AuthController.baseCookieOptions()` feeds it directly into the session JWT and 7-day refresh cookies (auth.controller.ts:406, used at 369 and 377), so both the transport flag and the anti-cookie-tossing prefix drop together — the exact session-fixation vector the module's own comments (oauth-state.ts:66-84) say `__Host-` exists to block. The self-hosting docs hand operators that shape (`http://localhost:3000/auth/github/callback` at self-hosting.md:42, `http://your-domain:3000/auth/github/callback` at :121) and concede the downgrade at :137-143. The only compensation is a single one-shot `logger.warn` in `GitHubAuthGuard.warnIfInsecureOrigin` (github-auth.guard.ts:263-273); grep shows `insecureProductionOrigin` has no other non-test caller, and main.ts emits no bootstrap warning, so deployments authenticating from existing cookies or API keys never see it. No refutation ground fits: the code is present as described, a log line plus a docs paragraph is not an enforced guard that makes the path unreachable, and session/refresh credentials transmitted without `Secure` plus a removed write-restriction control is sensitive-credential exposure and an auth weakness squarely in the security lane. Major severity (weakness requiring an operator misconfiguration that the docs themselves make likely, not yet a self-contained exploit).
